definitions.explanation: A literary たる-adjective describing a state, result, or condition that is grim, devastating, or pitiable. Almost always appears in the prenominal form {惨憺|さんたん}たる or in the set compound {苦心|くしん}{惨憺|さんたん}.

examples.japanese: {惨憺|さんたん}たる{結果|けっか}に{終|お}わった。
examples.english: It ended in a disastrous result.

examples.japanese: {現場|げんば}は{惨憺|さんたん}たる{有様|ありさま}だった。
examples.english: The scene was a wretched sight.

examples.japanese: {苦心|くしん}{惨憺|さんたん}の{末|すえ}、ようやく{完成|かんせい}にこぎつけた。
examples.english: After painstaking effort, we finally managed to complete it.

notes:
A literary たる-adjective derived from Classical Japanese. In modern usage it appears almost exclusively in the prenominal form {惨憺|さんたん}たる or in the fixed compound {苦心|くしん}{惨憺|さんたん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {惨憺|さんたん}たる{結果|けっか}: disastrous results
- {惨憺|さんたん}たる{有様|ありさま}: a wretched state
- {惨憺|さんたん}たる{光景|こうけい}: a grim scene
- {苦心|くしん}{惨憺|さんたん}: painstaking effort; toiling agonizingly

USAGE:
Never used as a plain predicate (×{惨憺|さんたん}だ is unnatural). Modern speakers use {悲惨|ひさん} or ひどい in everyday conversation; {惨憺|さんたん} sounds formal or literary.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悲惨|ひさん}: tragic; miserable — much more common in everyday speech
- {惨|みじ}め: miserable; pitiful — focuses on personal humiliation
- ひどい: terrible; awful — colloquial, very general
